goals: Isolate the mechanistic effect of soil clay content on surface runoff vs subsurface drainage partitioning
key_processes: Infiltration capacity as a function of soil texture

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly represents texture-dependent infiltration and drainage via Richards equation. Controlled experiment isolates clay effect by holding forcing, vegetation, and other factors constant.

answerable: Clay content control on infiltration capacity and runoff/recharge partitioning
Mechanistic response curve across sandy loam to silty clay textures

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 6 treatments span the 5-55% range at ~10% intervals, sufficient to resolve monotonic or threshold responses in partitioning without redundancy. Each treatment is one column.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Not spatial. Single representative location with uniform forcing. All columns identical except for clay content treatment.
sampling_strategy.replication: None. Controlled conditions eliminate stochastic variation; replication not needed for mechanism isolation.

sampling_plan.reason: Sandy loam baseline: high infiltration, minimal runoff, maximum drainage
Loam: moderate infiltration, beginning of runoff generation
Silt loam: reduced infiltration, increased surface runoff
Clay loam: low hydraulic conductivity, runoff-dominated partitioning
Silty clay loam: very low infiltration, high runoff, minimal drainage
Silty clay: near-impermeable, maximum runoff, negligible recharge

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: Uniform forcing (single representative climate), default vegetation, vary only clay content

requires_capabilities.capability: Custom soil texture specification per column
requires_capabilities.why: Must set clay % (and derived sand/silt) independently for each treatment column
requires_capabilities.blocks: Ability to implement the 6 clay-content treatments

requires_capabilities.why: All columns must receive identical meteorological forcing to isolate soil effect
requires_capabilities.blocks: Controlled-experiment validity (if forcing varies, confounds clay effect)

assumptions: ELM's Richards equation solver adequately represents texture-dependent infiltration and percolation across the clay range
Other soil properties (organic matter, structure) held at default/representative values
Vegetation type/LAI held constant across treatments
Single representative forcing climate is sufficient (no need to test clay effect across multiple climates)
Spin-up not critical for partitioning comparison (or brief spin-up applied uniformly to all treatments)
open_questions: What forcing period/climate should be used? (Suggest a moderate-precipitation regime to see both runoff and drainage)
Should sand/silt be adjusted proportionally as clay varies, or held constant?
Is a short spin-up (e.g. 2 years) needed to equilibrate soil moisture, or can we compare from cold start?
What output frequency is desired for partitioning analysis (daily, monthly)?
